[3dprintdeals] Unraid is great.
The UI is really user-friendly, whether you're a beginner or an advanced user who just doesn't want to muck around.
But with AI agents these days, I'd also consider free alternatives like TrueNAS SCALE.
Lately, I've just been getting my agent to set up Docker containers, so drive pools and raid would be a breeze.
Also, with drive/ram pricing right now it's a tough time to setup a new server so using old hardware is a good option.
[3dprintdeals] Flash Drive Boot
They have added option for NVME boot, but typical setup is a USB flash drive, so use a high quality drive and set up backups.
[twitch1979] Can the NVME boot also be your parity or cache drive, or would that not be recommended?
[FlipCrank] While my experience with Unraid was fine, I didn't agree with the pricing model. I went down the path of OMV + mergerfs which was a sufficient alternative for my needs.
[3dprintdeals] Definitely threw a lot of people off. I have gone over a year without upgrading though and I'm on the perpetual license.
Can also add snapRAID for parity protection
[MasterScythe] Especially now MergerFS and SnapRAID have such beautiful WebUI's.
[tanksinatra] No discount on lifetime is disappointing.
I tried Unraid and it was ok, but the new pricing model scared me off. I went with SnapRAID + Drivepool instead. Setting it up with an AI agent is even more user friendly than Unraid. And it's a fraction of the price.
Personally I'm waiting for the HexOS + ZFS AnyRAID. It's a exciting feature that merges mixed size drive support together with the security and data protection of ZFS. I reckon Unraid will be in trouble if that comes out.
[3dprintdeals] If you want to have mixed drive sizes. AnyRAID is still not fully implemented yet.
[S Baldrick] TrueNAS is a bit of a pain to setup IMO, especially with the granular dataset permissions
Source: using TrueNAS Scale
[undadog] been on my watchlist for a while now.
thanks!
